diagnosis.bottleneck: The query performs a full scan of the promotion table with a filter on p_channel_tv = 'N'. The scan (node 1) reads all Parquet row groups because the table is not partitioned or sorted by p_channel_tv, making predicate pushdown ineffective at the file/row-group level. The downstream aggregation (nodes 4, 6) and shuffle (node 5) are trivial in comparison.

hypotheses.claim: No known pattern matched; the plan's most expensive operator is the candidate.

The scan reads the entire promotion table because p_channel_tv is not a partition column and Parquet row-group statistics do not prune any row groups; rewriting the table to partition by p_channel_tv or sorting by it would allow file-level pruning and reduce I/O.

The filter operator (node 2) re-evaluates the same predicate after the scan, indicating that the pushed filter may not be fully applied at the Parquet page level (e.g., due to missing statistics or dictionary encoding); collecting column statistics or using a more selective predicate could reduce CPU time spent filtering.

The partial hash aggregate (node 4) processes a large number of rows because the filter selectivity is high (many rows have p_channel_tv = 'N'), making the counting loop the dominant CPU cost; if the selectivity is indeed high, a materialized view or pre-aggregated table would avoid scanning the detail rows.
